characterization_methods.key_findings: Regardless of Si content, no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite had taken place.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine whether spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering occurred in the solution-treated austenite

characterization_methods.key_findings: 200 ± 10 BHN for the solution-treated 0.59% Si, 0.002% P steel.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Converted from Rockwell B and C scale measurements

characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated 0.59% Si, 0.002% P steel DFT = 715 kJ/m².
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fatigue precracked Charpy specimens; high loading rate
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure dynamic fracture toughness (critical J integral near onset of stable crack growth)
characterization_methods.technique: Instrumented Charpy impact test (Schindler single-specimen method)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ASPEX scanning electron microscope (FEI Company, Hillsboro, OR) with PICA 1020 software
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.59% Si steel had much larger porosity (micro-defects) than the 1.07% and 1.56% Si steels; total inclusion density 62–78 inclusions/mm² among the three low-P Si steels.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine inclusion type/distribution and their effect on CVN impact energy

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Combined with TEM, 3-D APT, and XRD experiments; ab initio results showed Si increases carbon activity in austenite and stabilizes κ-carbide at higher temperatures.

interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase fully austenitic matrix; no secondary-phase interfaces present in the solution-treated condition.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite in the solution-treated condition.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution treatment at 1050°C for 2 h followed by water quench to produce a fully austenitic matrix.

measurement_conditions.test_standard: Brinell hardness (3000 kg) converted from Rockwell B and C scale measurements

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Dynamic fracture toughness defined as critical value of the J integral near onset of stable crack growth
measurement_conditions.test_standard: Schindler single-specimen method; ASTM E 1820; ASTM E 813

defects.porosity: Porosity (micro-defects) in the 0.59% Si steel was more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix; XRD and TEM confirmed no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite in the solution-treated condition.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemistry (Table I, wt%): Si 0.59, C 0.95, Mn 30.35, P 0.002, S 0.006, Mo 0.54, Al 8.74, Cu 0.01 (balance Fe) [b0013].

Abstract: solution-treated cast steels in the 0.59–1.56% Si range show high work-hardening rates, elongations up to 64%, room-temperature CVN up to 200 J, and dynamic fracture toughness over 700 kJ/m²; Si additions in this range have no significant effect on solution-treated mechanical properties [b0004].
